title: CAPEX add-line-item design
purpose: Design the add-line UX for the C.01..C.18 CAPEX sheet. The UX is data-only in 57A-5 (data-capex-add-line="<code>"). This PR designs the JS hook, the numeric impact, and the persistence approach. No runtime implementation in 57A-6.

ux_flow.discovery: Small '+ Add line' button at the right edge of each C.01..C.16 category section band.
ux_flow.click: JS hook reads the parent category code from data-capex-add-line="<code>", finds the next available sub-line code, inserts an empty input row.
ux_flow.edit: User types a label and an amount. The amount input uses the existing input_field_template="capex_{code}_keur".
ux_flow.save: Standard CAPEX update flow applies the new line.

next_available_code: Read existing sub-line codes for the category (e.g. C.01.01, C.01.02, C.01.03); assign the next available (C.01.04).

options_considered.name: option_a_schema_change
options_considered.description: Replace fixed field set with list of sub-line items in CapexStructure. Breaking change.
options_considered.rejected_reason: Breaking change to persistence layer; not minimal.

options_considered.name: option_b_in_memory_only
options_considered.description: New line is preserved across the user's session but not saved to disk.
options_considered.rejected_reason: User loses work on next session open. Bad UX.

options_considered.name: option_c_hybrid
options_considered.description: New table capex_sub_lines keyed on project_id + category_code. Does not change CapexStructure shape.
options_considered.selected_reason: Migration-friendly; does not break existing CapexStructure; allows free add/remove.

persistence_approach.implementation_note: The capex_detail_items builder in app/ui/project_context.py::_build_capex_detail_items would augment each category's children tuple with rows from capex_sub_lines for the current project. No change to CapexStructure shape.

stop_and_document: The migration file and the persistence-layer changes are explicitly out of scope for 57A-6. The 57A-6 PR is design only — no migration, no persistence change, no runtime change. The actual implementation must come in a future runtime PR (e.g. 57A-8 or later) that explicitly scopes the migration.
